text:
Cale Makar will miss about two weeks with a soft tissue injury that coach Jared Bednar said he had been playing through before it got worse in Ottawa, the same game that cost Nathan MacKinnon a month. Bednar told the Denver Post he isn't worried about it lingering, and a light stretch of schedule (three games before late November, as Corey Masisak noted) softens the blow.

He goes out playing like Makar: 23 points in 19 games, 18 of them assists, and the Avalanche hold 57.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice. His five goals have come on 3.03 expected, a little hot, but the playmaking carries it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.0 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 97th percentile among defensemen, and he still owns the hardest shot in our NHL Edge data. Our range for his scoring rate sits below the current pace, so some cooling was likely anyway. The bigger question is what Colorado looks like for two weeks without its top defenseman and top center at once.
